We use the Pythagorean identity:

$$
{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x=1
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }({cos}^{3}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡x({cos}^{2}⁡x+{sin}^{2}⁡x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,{|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡0 \\  & =0-0 \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
